literal: Having feigned anger, shall we obtain indeed, forehead to perspire, in the reunion that arose relish?
translation: Will we ever obtain again, by feigning anger, that exquisite relish that arose during our reunion, which made her forehead perspire?
modern: நெற்றியில் வியர்வை அரும்பும்படி நாம் கூடி மகிழ்ந்தபோது உண்டான அந்த இன்பத்தை (சுவையை), மீண்டும் நாம் ஊடல் கொள்வதன் மூலம் பெற முடியுமோ?
explanation: This couplet describes the intense pleasure of reunion after a brief period of feigned anger (ūṭal). The word 'உப்பு' (literally salt) is used here in the sense of 'relish' or 'savoury delight', comparing the pleasure of love to the essential flavor that salt adds to food. The lover wonders if they can recreate that passionate moment of reunion—which was so intense that it made the beloved's forehead perspire—simply by starting another playful argument. It highlights how temporary disagreements serve to heighten physical and emotional intimacy.
